findings.F1: A coin's 14-day return, in units of its 30-day volatility, predicts its excess return over the next 10 days, and the effect grows with the move. On the non-overlapping 10-day grid with all 6 coins pooled, the standardised product has mean 0.078 (t 2.60, 1,403 cases, 5 of 6 coins positive). The largest-move third of cases has an unusual move of 268 bps (t 3.40, 468 cases) and a strength of 0.16, which is 3 times the usual 0.05 (F10). Its total move of 294 bps is about 15 times this backtest's 19 bps round trip.
findings.F2: That 10-day momentum is not steady over time. The unusual move is 215 bps (t 3.37, 707 cases) in windows w13 to w24 but -47 bps (t -0.91, 696 cases) in w1 to w12. The 7-day return behaves the same way at 10 days: 143 bps (t 2.23) late against 25 bps (t 0.49) early.
findings.F3: Momentum that pays at 5 to 10 days is gone by 20 days, the tested horizon. The 28-day volatility-scaled return gives t 2.20 at 5 days and at 10 days, but t 0.72 at 20 days (539 cases). The tested idea's own size at 20 days is -0.44 % per case, which is -2.3 times the cost of a trade.
findings.F4: The tested idea's gradient points the right way but is weak. The 28-day momentum's product with the 20-day excess return has t 1.71 in the calmest third of volatility (182 cases), t 0.46 in the middle third and t -0.28 in the most volatile third.
findings.F5: A coin's one-day move reverses the next day, and the reversal grows with the move. The 1-day volatility-scaled return times the next day's excess return has t -4.19 (14,500 days), negative on all 6 coins. The reversal is 10, 11 and 28 bps per case from the smallest to the largest third of moves. In the largest third it is positive on all 6 coins (6 to 64 bps), with t 3.76 in w1 to w12 and t 1.81 in w13 to w24. At 28 bps it is only about 1.5 times the cost of a round trip.
findings.F6: Daily excess returns differ by weekday. Wednesday is -30 bps (t -2.70, 2,489 days) and negative on all 6 coins and in both halves; Monday is -24 bps (t -2.53); Thursday is +25 bps (t 2.63) and Friday +30 bps (t 3.76). This is a calendar condition, not a graded situation, and I tested about 7 weekdays among many angles.
findings.F7: The book's yearly mean daily return trails holding in 5 of 8 years and beats it only in 2018, 2022 and 2025. In 2018 the book made 0.10 % a day against -0.35 % for holding; in 2023 it made -0.17 % against +0.15 %.

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's 14-day return, measured in units of its 30-day daily volatility, the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: Momentum bets on the last two weeks' move should be held for about ten days rather than three to four weeks, because the move they capture has faded by then.
ideas.name: two-week momentum, ten-day hold

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day return against its 30-day daily volatility, the more its return over the next day goes the opposite way.
ideas.consequence: A trader should lean against a coin's unusually large daily moves for one day, and avoid chasing them.
ideas.name: large-day next-day reversal
